title: Meet the pawn
objectives: Understand pawns move forward but capture diagonally

steps.text: A pawn moves straight ahead, one square at a time — except on its very first move, when it may move two squares. It never moves backward.

steps.prompt: Move the pawn forward two squares — its first move from the starting rank.

hints.text: A pawn on its starting square may move one or two squares straight ahead.
The pawn advances from e2 to e4 — its two-square first move.

feedback.default: A pawn moves straight ahead — never sideways or diagonally unless it's capturing.

steps.successExplanation: That's a legal pawn move. Only on its very first move can a pawn advance two squares instead of one.

steps.text: A pawn captures differently from how it moves: diagonally, one square forward-left or forward-right — never straight ahead.

steps.prompt: Capture the black pawn diagonally ahead of you.

hints.text: A pawn captures diagonally, one square ahead — never straight forward.
The black pawn is one square diagonally ahead of yours.
Your pawn captures on d5 — diagonally forward, one square.

feedback.default: A pawn can only capture diagonally, one square ahead — it can't capture something directly in front of it.

steps.successExplanation: exd5 captures the pawn. This is the one time a pawn's move and its capture use different directions — straight to move, diagonal to capture.

steps.prompt: A pawn can capture a piece directly in front of it.

feedback.default: A pawn moves straight but captures diagonally — a piece directly ahead actually blocks it.

steps.successExplanation: Right — a piece directly ahead blocks a pawn's forward move entirely; it can never be captured that way.
